content_html_sanitized:
The other day I saw a story about all of the things that were once commonplace, but have disappeared from our lives and vocabulary. Some examples were “collect calls”, “Roladex”, and “pagers”. There are many more, but thinking about them makes me feel old.

 

However, there are other things that we really should not forget about. One is “Ditch Weed”, which today is just slang for really bad weed.

 

By the time I started doing MarijuanaNews, it had become a U.S. military program to eradicate feral hemp that was growing in ditches around farms across the country. How did that happen?

 

After the passing of the Marihuana Tax Act of 1937 at the bottom of the Great Depression, agricultural hemp production almost completely disappeared in America. But when World War Two started, the U.S. lost access to Philippine fiber that was needed for the war effort. So the United States government reversed course and encouraged American farmers to grow Hemp for Victory, which,of course, they did.

 

After the war, hemp was once again just the evil marijuana, and the farmers went back to whatever else they were growing. However, the seeds from the plants were still spreading in the ditches around the fields now growing corn, or wheat or whatever, but no one cared. Well, the birds did, and helped spread the “bird seed”.

 

Enter The Drug War! At some point some in the 1970s city slickers, AKA hippies, saw the leaves and either thought it was “marijuana”, or thought other city slickers might buy it. So every fall, when the plants had flowered some would harvest the ditches, and eventually this was a threat to America’s children. Call in the National Guard!!!

 

Yes, this really happened.

But where did the history go? Down the Memory Hole of incompetent journalism that continues to make marijuana prohibition possible.
